&api-questions;
The nbfx Annotations API defines the annotations and layer paths with which the pure-JavaFX NetBeans frontend declares its registration-based components: actions, menu and tool bar references, views, status bar elements, property editors, options panels, project types and wizards.
The module contains only SOURCE-retention annotations, the FxLayer path constants, and annotation processors built on org.openide.filesystems.annotations.LayerGeneratingProcessor. The processors emit META-INF/generated-layer.xml fragments under the NbFx/ paths; the runtime JavaFX presenters read those paths from the module layer. This reproduces the NetBeans declarative-registration model without depending on the Swing-bound org.openide.awt action processor.
Primary use cases:
A module declares an action with @FxActionRegistration and places it in a menu, tool bar or context menu with @FxActionReference.
A module declares a dockable view with @FxViewRegistration.
A module contributes a status bar element with @FxStatusRegistration.
A module contributes a property editor with @FxPropertyEditorRegistration.
The processors are covered by unit tests that assert the generated layer fragments for a sample annotated source. The module API is marked under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.
A JDK is required, to compile the annotation processors. JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
Only com.gluonhq.netbeans.nbfx.annotations is public, so other modules can use the annotations and the layer path constants. The processor implementations are an implementation detail and are not exported.
The processors are discovered by the compiler through the META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor service, generated by @ServiceProvider(service=Processor.class). The runtime presenters discover the generated layer entries with Lookups.forPath.

Yes. The processors create folders and files under NbFx/ in the generated layer: Actions, Menus, Toolbars, ContextMenus, Views, Status, PropertyEditors, Options, Projects and Wizards.
